# Objective

In this file, we will use Generalized Extreme Value Distributions and Generalized Pareto Distributions to try to find an appropriate distributional fit of extreme precipitation in Asheville, NC. Eventually, we will use this to attempt to predict the extreme precipitation associated with Hurricane Helene.

# Programming

## Package & Data Setup
```{python}
# Package Import
import pandas as pd
import geopandas as gpd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import plotly.express as px
import plotly.graph_objects as go
from plotly.subplots import make_subplots
import os
import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

# Data Import
asheville_df = pd.read_csv("../data/ghcn_roi_daily_data/Asheville.csv")
```

## Create Plots to show Inadequacy of Typical Distributional Fits

```{python}
# Check an exponential fit:
## Fit exponential
precip = asheville_df["precipitation"].dropna()
loc, scale = stats.expon.fit(precip, floc=0)
lambda_hat = 1 / scale
print(f"Estimated rate (λ): {lambda_hat:.4f}")
print(f"Estimated mean (1/λ): {scale:.4f}")

# Visualize fit vs. data
x = np.linspace(0, precip.max(), 300)
pdf_exp = stats.expon.pdf(x, loc=loc, scale=scale)

plt.figure(figsize=(8,5))
plt.hist(precip, bins=50, density=True, alpha=0.5, label="Empirical histogram")
plt.plot(x, pdf_exp, "r-", lw=2, label=f"Exponential fit (λ={lambda_hat:.3f})")
plt.xlabel("Precipitation (mm)")
plt.ylabel("Density")
plt.title("Exponential Fit vs. Observed Precipitation, Asheville, NC")
plt.legend()
plt.grid(alpha=0.3)
plt.show()

# Compare expected vs. observed tail counts
lower, upper = 44.7, 200

## empirical count
n_total = len(precip)
observed_count = np.sum((precip >= lower) & (precip <= upper))

## exponential probability mass in that region
p_interval = stats.expon.cdf(upper, loc=loc, scale=scale) - stats.expon.cdf(lower, loc=loc, scale=scale)
expected_count = n_total * p_interval

print(f"Observed count in [{lower}, {upper}]: {observed_count}")
print(f"Expected (Exponential) count: {expected_count:.1f}")
print(f"Observed / Expected ratio: {observed_count / expected_count:.2f}")
```

## Get Extreme Value Distribution Fits

```{python}
## WE WILL ATTEMPT TO MODEL THE TOP 1% OF EXTREME VALUES
# Find 99th percentile of daily precipitation
precip = asheville_df["precipitation"].dropna()
quantile_99 = precip.quantile(0.99)
print("99th quantile of precipitation:", quantile_99, "mm")
```
